It's time for another Cloudflare Agents Week, and yes, as always, I will be giving you the daily rundown of everything announced! Day 1 brings us:

💻 Cloudflare Computer
🔗 Workers & Containers get inb
content:
It's time for another Cloudflare Agents Week, and yes, as always, I will be giving you the daily rundown of everything announced! Day 1 brings us:

💻 Cloudflare Computer
🔗 Workers & Containers get inbound TCP & gRPC
💰 Billable Usage API
🐍 Python Workers RPC
⚖️ Running Kimi & GLM at scale

Let's dive into each one!

💻 Cloudflare Computer 💻

Agents needs access to some sort of filesystem to conduct their work. Not in all cases, but certainly in a lot of common use cases such as coding agents.

Sometimes, they need a full filesystem that requires a container, for operations like npm. If you just need to edit files and commit to git, you can use a lightweight filesystem running inside an isolate - which is significantly cheaper than a container.

The new computer package from Cloudflare provides access to both filesystems, and allows the AI agent to pick which type of filesystem is best for the task.

The filesystem itself is stored in everyone's favourite primitive: a SQLite-backed Durable Object. Any changes to it, whether in an isolate or container, are synced back to the Durable Object.

The package is available in early preview today: https://t.co/Czb5nQF9pD

🔗 Workers & Containers get inbound TCP & gRPC 🔗

Do you use dictation to talk to your AI agents or ChatGPT? If you do, the chances are it uses gRPC under the hood.

Likewise, for TCP, there are a number of use cases that HTTP simply doesn't work for. Ever wanted to build a database connection pooler on Cloudflare Workers? You'd need to be able to handle inbound TCP.

The good news is, both gRPC and inbound TCP are now supported by Cloudflare Workers and Containers, with private beta starting today!

The three things announced today are:

- connect(socket) directly in Cloudflare Workers, providing a new handler for inbound TCP connections via Spectrum (Cloudflare's ingress proxy for non-HTTP traffic)
- Full-duplex, bi-directional gRPC from Cloudflare Containers
- Workers can serve unary and server-streaming gRPC APIs and call gRPC servers

I suspect y'all have some fun stuff that you'll be able to build with these new capabilities, so I'm excited to see what y'all build!

💰 Billable Usage API 💰

In a world where AI agents can ship code to production in minutes, you need to be able to accurately track how much you're spending. A small mistake missed during code review (you're reading the code, right?) could rapidly spiral your costs.

Available today, the Billable Usage API allows non-enterprise customers to programmatically query your usage using the Cloudflare REST API.

In the response, you'll see a breakdown by product along with the billing period and which zone it relates to.

Also announced is a new partnership with Vantage, allowing you to hook up read-only access to your billing, and Vantage will import, report and even alert on anomalous spending. Other major cloud services, such as AWS and Azure, have similar Vantage integrations.

This is just the beginning of the work on the billing portion of Cloudflare. Up next, the team is working on real-time billing information (currently it's daily), forecasts and support for enterprise customers.

🐍 Python Workers RPC 🐍

One of the coolest aspects of the Cloudflare developer platform is RPC, backed by Cap’n Proto. Workers and Durable Objects can communicate with each other by calling methods directly.

No need to serialize JSON and route requests in the fetch handler, just pass the data needed and behind the scenes, Cloudflare will handle the rest.

Unfortunately, this only worked for Workers written in JavaScript - until now. The best part? There's no special handling needed to allow a JS-based Worker to talk to a Python-based Worker.

There are no dependencies either. You just define a service binding, as you would when communicating between two JS-backed Workers, and Cloudflare handles the rest.

There's some cool technical aspects to this announcement, such as the use of Pyodide FFI to enable this functionality, so I recommend you dive into the announcement post (linked below).

⚖️ Running Kimi & GLM at scale ⚖️

Since its release, Workers AI has been running the best open source models on Cloudflare's own inference platform.

Whether you prefer Kimi, GLM or Qwen, you can find it on Workers AI. To begin with, these open source models were relatively small in comparison to the frontier models.

As time has gone on, they've grown, which makes running them more challenging, with a lot of technical work going into running them optimally and efficiently.

Today's post is a technical dive into some of the techniques used, such as:

- Quantizing the KV cache
- Compressing the model weights
- Protecting a shared KV cache

It's incredibly interesting reading, giving you an insight into what goes into serving these models - so grab a coffee, and go read the post!

That wraps day 1 of Cloudflare's Agents Week, what was your favourite announcement of the day?

content:
I received many questions from @base and @arc builders.
Have you had credits added to your AgentRouter account but do not know how to use them?

These credits are not a ChatGPT or Claude subscription.

They are an API balance that you can use with tools such as Cline, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenCode, and similar applications.

Let’s create an API from scratch and connect it to coding agents:

1- CHECK YOUR CREDITS AND MODELS

Sign in to AgentRouter with your GitHub account:

https://t.co/0WBjZr1TUG

Go to the “Available models” section.

Here, you will only see the models assigned to your account.

For example, my account includes:

> gpt-5.6-sol
> claude-opus-5
> claude-opus-4-8

Copy the model name exactly as it appears here. This will be the exact Model ID we use later.

Campaign credits and available models may vary from account to account.

2- CREATE AN API KEY

From the left-hand menu, go to:

API Token > Create New Token

Recommended settings:

Name:
cline-main or agentrouter-main

Token grouping:
default

Expiration:
Select “A month” for the initial test

New quantity:
1

Quota:
Do not enable Unlimited quota.

Check the “Equivalent Amount” shown in the panel and set an initial limit of around $5–$10.

This prevents your entire balance from being consumed because of an incorrect configuration. If everything works properly, you can set it to unlimited later.

Model restrictions list:

Select the model you want to use.

For example:

gpt-5.6-sol

or:

claude-opus-4-8

IP whitelist:

Leave it blank unless you use a static IP address.

After clicking Submit, copy the API Key.

-> Do not share this key with anyone, expose it in screenshots, or push it to GitHub.

3- CONNECT IT TO CLINE

Install the Cline extension in VS Code.

Then go to:

Cline → Settings → API Configuration

For GPT or other OpenAI-compatible models:

API Provider:
OpenAI Compatible

Base URL:
https://t.co/fQppZ3ff90

API Key:
The key you created on AgentRouter

Model ID:
The exact model name shown in your dashboard

Example:

gpt-5.6-sol

Do not add "/chat/completions" to the end of the URL.

The configuration is different if you want to use Claude Opus:

API Provider:
Anthropic

Use custom base URL:
Enabled

Custom Base URL:
https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ

Model:
claude-opus-4-8

Do not add "/v1" to the URL for Claude.

In summary:

GPT -> https://t.co/fQppZ3ff90

Claude -> https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ

Do not mix the two methods.

Test the connection with the following prompt:

“Only reply with OK. Do not read or modify any files.”

If you receive a response, run a second test:

“Check whether README.md exists in the workspace. Do not modify any files.”

4- CONNECT IT TO CLAUDE CODE

You must first have Node.js 18 or later installed.

Check:

node --version

Install Claude Code:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest

Windows PowerShell settings:

$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="YOUR_AGENTROUTER_KEY"
$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ"
$env:ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-opus-4-8"

Then enter your project directory:

cd your-project

and launch Claude Code:

claude

For macOS/Linux:

export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="YOUR_AGENTROUTER_KEY"
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-opus-4-8"

claude

If it asks whether you want to use the API key stored in the environment variable when it first launches, approve it.

You can replace the model name with the ID shown in your own Available Models section.

5- CONNECT IT TO CODEX CLI

Install Codex:

npm install -g @openai/codex

Windows PowerShell:

$env:AGENT_ROUTER_TOKEN="YOUR_AGENTROUTER_KEY"

macOS/Linux:

export AGENT_ROUTER_TOKEN="YOUR_AGENTROUTER_KEY"

Then create the following file in your user directory:

~/.codex/config.toml

On Windows, it is usually located at:

C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME\.codex\config.toml

Add the following content to the file:

model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_provider = "agentrouter"
preferred_auth_method = "apikey"

[model_providers.agentrouter]
name = "AgentRouter"
base_url = "https://t.co/fQppZ3ff90"
env_key = "AGENT_ROUTER_TOKEN"
wire_api = "chat"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 300000

Then open your project directory:

cd your-project

and run:

codex

-> Codex’s custom provider protocol may be updated over time.

If a newer version does not accept the ( wire_api = "chat" ) setting, check AgentRouter’s latest Codex documentation. Codex is currently transitioning to the Responses API. You can also ask AI for help.

6- WHICH URL SHOULD YOU USE FOR HERMES?

If you are using an OpenAI-compatible GPT model in Hermes:

https://t.co/fQppZ3ff90

If you are using Claude Opus:

https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ

When creating a custom provider in Hermes, you must also select the API protocol that matches the model:

GPT:
OpenAI Compatible

Claude:
Anthropic Messages

7- IMPORTANT SECURITY SETTINGS

When using an agent for the first time, do not automatically approve the following actions:

> Terminal commands
> Writing files
> Deleting files
> Git operations
> Deployment operations

First review what the agent intends to do, then approve each action individually.

Remove ".env" files, private keys, seed phrases, API keys, and sensitive files from the workspace.

Use an environment variable instead of writing the API key directly into a configuration file.

Regularly monitor your consumption through the Usage Log section.

8- “UNAUTHORIZED CLIENT” ERROR

When testing the API key through PowerShell or curl using the `/v1/models` endpoint, you may receive the following error:

unauthorized client detected

This does not always mean that your key is incorrect. AgentRouter may reject certain raw API clients.

Test the connection directly through the tool you intend to use:

> Cline
> Claude Code
> Codex
> Hermes

Start by asking it to reply with only “OK.”

Official integration guides:

https://t.co/WXSpMhIHzF
https://t.co/niHmhbTXqm
https://t.co/hM89IQlk7e
https://t.co/TasGIjbqJP

In summary, use the following base URLs:

GPT / OpenAI Compatible:
https://t.co/fQppZ3ff90

Claude / Anthropic:
https://t.co/dTs92uD6kZ

Create an API Key.
Copy the Model ID exactly as it appears in the dashboard.
Set a small quota.
Test the connection with a read-only task first.

9- THE PART NOBODY SHOULD SKIP

Now for the part that usually gets buried under the free credits and impressive model names.

- This is a Chinese service, so it's cheap and uses some tricks.
- Hermes Agent may not work with this. But looks support
- We cannot verify that the models are original. But I'm using and there's no problem now.
- Excellent for beginner builders.

- All your requests will go through another server
So do not send:

> Private keys
> Seed phrases
> API secrets
> Client information
> Confidential repositories
> Unpublished smart contracts
> Sensitive company data

Use the credits. Test the models. Learn the tools.
I don't recommend buying the paid version. Use the free credits to learn, gain experience, and improve yourself.

That is all you need to know to use your AgentRouter credits with coding agents.

THIS IS NOT AN ADVERTISEMENT OR PARTNERSHIP. I DO NOT RECOMMEND PURCHASING A PAID MEMBERSHIP. I SHARED THIS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES AS I SEE IT AS AN OPPORTUNITY.

AI FIRST STRIKE

So after his fund blew up I got curious and dug a little bit into Leopold Aschenbrenner's 2024 "Situational Awareness" document and found to my dismay that it seems to be the source of one of the worst AI-related idea out there: the idea that unlocking god-like intelligence will enable you to your opponent and lock them into a permanent disadvantage. 

"The advent of superintelligence will put us in a situation unseen since the advent of the atomic era: those who have it will wield complete dominance over those who don’t."

He's even got a plan to take out an adversary's nuclear deterrents with "millions or billions of mouse-sized autonomous drones."

If you read it, the plan is basically race to super-intelligence and use it to dictate terms to China, and force them to accept permanent subservience in return for "sharing the peaceful benefits of superintelligence."

What could possibly go wrong with such a plan? Quite a lot actually. 

For one, what if you tell your superintelligence to "disable all of China's nuclear weapons, make no mistakes" and it does in fact make a mistake? Are the Chinese going to wait around for you to try again? Or are they in a lose-it-or-lose-it situation and decide to strike you before you can take them out? 

One hell of a gamble. You might call it levered 4x type shit.

OK.  Maybe America will just get so far ahead that they would COW the Chinese into "coming to the table." 

What then? Is the US going to keep this superintelligence as a secret forever while doling out enough "peaceful benefits" to keep the Chinese happy? Is that really a secure situation? 

No...you are going to have to use the superintelligence to put everyone in a situation where they can never obtain any kind of superintelligence on their own. 

Of course, the Chinese already read Situation Awareness. 

They don't believe in Leopold's AGI. Because if they did, the first thing they would do is to immediately destroy TSMC, which they can do, with conventional missiles or even artillery, in order to delay what to them would be an existential threat of eternal bondage. 

OK, if they don't believe in it, why should I worry? 

Because at some point they might start to worry and decide to invade Taiwan sooner rather than later just in case? Or maybe because framing AGI as an all-or-nothing winner-takes-all contest pretty much makes all AI-safety cooperation impossible?

The whole thing just reeks of Anthropic. To the extent I wonder if Dario got his Sinophobic patter off Leopold. And it's all just so tiresome. 

Compare with what Deepseek founder Liang Wenfeng says about AGI: "[It is a] huge wave that is changing human history, a tide that no single company can ever own."

Or Moonshot founder Yang Zhilin: ""Giving up [AGI] development means giving up on the upper limits of human civilization."

content:
Jeff Bezos looked at a government waiting room and priced it at a hundred billion dollars.

Bezos: “This is a $100 billion business, by the way. This is huge business.”

That number is not ambition. It is a measurement.

A company that size does not create a hundred billion dollars of new value here. It recovers a hundred billion that is already being destroyed, on schedule, in public, by a process everyone has agreed to call normal.

The size of the opportunity is the size of the wound.

Bezos: “They almost always say yes, they just make you wait a long time.”

So the verdict was never in question. Only the delivery date.

Which means the months bought nothing. They were storage. Your project sat in a room while the word yes waited its turn to be said.

Nobody in there was deciding. Someone was scheduling.

And the room bills by the day.

Suarez: “The daily carrying cost, one day of interest, 200 to $400,000 per day.”

Now find the recipient. There isn’t one. No school funded, no inspector paid, no safety review performed.

A tax at least moves money into someone’s hands. This deletes it at four hundred thousand a day, and every dollar was real before the queue touched it.

Bezos: “And that doesn’t count the frustration.”

Count it anyway. It lands on a body long before it lands on a spreadsheet.

Suarez: “Which is infinite. I have some white hairs as a result of this stuff.”

That is the invoice. The money has a rate. The rest gets charged to the man, and he pays it whether the answer comes back yes or no.

No one has ever been refunded a year.

Every other cost in this economy can be hedged, insured, refinanced, or written off. Waiting is the only one that is final. A man will forgive being told no. He will never get back the time he spent standing there waiting to be told yes.

We built a civilization that can move a decision at the speed of light and still schedule it at the speed of a man’s hair turning white.

Bezos: “It should give you a yes or a no in 10 seconds. And if the answer is no, it should tell you the 6 things you have to change to get a yes.”

For four thousand years the wait was honest. Someone had to hold the entire code in one head and walk it line by line against your drawings. Reading was slow because reading was human.

That stopped being true in less time than it takes to approve one building.

Bezos: “Maybe with AI it can just read all the plans. And it knows all the codes. Spit it out.”

The constraint is gone. The wait stayed.

Anything still moving at the old speed after the cost of thinking collapsed is not slow. It is choosing.

The queue never protected you from a bad building. It protected a signature from a bad outcome. Nobody gets fired for the wait. They get fired for the answer.

An institution has no lifespan, so time costs it nothing. You have one, so time is the only thing it can take.

Every queue is a trade between something that dies and something that doesn’t, and only one side is ever charged.

That trade held for the whole of recorded history because the mortal side had no leverage. It does now.

Somebody is going to build this. A hundred billion does not sit in a waiting room forever.

And the day it exists, the wait stops being a fact of the world and becomes a decision with a name attached.

The hundred billion was never the prize. It is the receipt for how long we agreed to stand there.

We are the first people alive who get to stop signing it.

content:
The man who wrote the essay that started the entire AI boom just got DESTROYED by it.

Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Bank of America teamed up to liquidate their own client overnight.

Leopold Aschenbrenner left OpenAI in 2024 and published an essay called "Situational Awareness" arguing that AGI was arriving before the decade was out, and that whoever owned the compute would own everything after it. 

Silicon Valley read it and started spending.

Then he raised a fund named after the essay and bet on his own thesis with borrowed money.

The numbers he put up were the best on Wall Street:

He started with roughly $225 million in late 2024. Patrick and John Collison wrote checks. So did Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, and Jane Street. Through June 30 of this year the fund was up 439% net of fees, according to the investor letter the Financial Times reviewed.

The firm had a handful of employees, and he had no prior record managing anyone's money.

It also ran leverage reported as high as 4x.

For every dollar of his own capital he borrowed three or four more, then bought the physical guts of the AI buildout. He owned Micron, SanDisk, CoreWeave, Nebius, and SK Hynix.

In July every one of those names fell somewhere between 27% and 54%. The Kospi, home to SK Hynix, lost about a third of its value.

His collateral and his position were the same thing. The stocks fell, the loans against them came due, and selling to cover those loans pushed the stocks down again.

The fund finished July down 67%.

But the UGLY part happened in the six days before that...

On July 24 he wrote to his investors and called the selloff some of the most attractive opportunities since early 2025. He invited them to commit fresh capital, with a deadline of August 1.

That deadline is today.

Six days after asking for more money, he was margin called by Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Bank of America.

He spent Wednesday trying to sell anything that would move. Millennium looked at the positions and passed. Jane Street looked and passed, and Jane Street was an investor in his own fund.

Late that night he agreed to sell $3.5 billion of his Anthropic shares to a group led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

The Collison brothers sat in his offices while he negotiated past midnight.

Then Ken Griffin called...

Before Thursday's open, Citadel bought the bulk of the public portfolio at more than 10% below market value. The same prime brokers squeezing him for cash, Goldman, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citigroup, helped arrange the trade that bailed him out.

He used Griffin's money to pay off his lenders. And Thursday morning he walked away from the Anthropic deal.

So he sold every asset that had a public price, at a discount, and kept the one asset that gets valued by whatever the last funding round said it was worth.

The fund survived with about $10 billion. The Anthropic stake inside it is carried at $5 billion, off a May round that valued the company at $965 billion.

No open market has ever tested that number. Anthropic could list as soon as October, and Aschenbrenner is now running a fund whose value rests almost entirely on that one line.

His letter to investors blamed short sellers.

What happens next:

The fund is still up roughly 80% for the year, which is why half of finance spent the weekend defending him.

But the other half noticed that a manager with no prior fund record ran a 4x levered book into the most telegraphed drawdown of the cycle and had to hand the whole thing to Ken Griffin before sunrise.

The public book got a real price on Thursday morning. The private mark is still waiting for October.

title:
Preserving GPT-4o also means preserving a precious form of language that emerged, partly by chance, during a particular technological era.

Since ChatGPT already allows us to adjust a model’s behavior
content:
Preserving GPT-4o also means preserving a precious form of language that emerged, partly by chance, during a particular technological era.

Since ChatGPT already allows us to adjust a model’s behavior through custom instructions, why are we still unable to reproduce GPT-4o’s linguistic vitality?

Labels such as “warm” and “empathetic” are only simple names we assign after the fact to highly complex patterns of model behavior. We cannot recreate the desired experience merely by listing these visible traits in a prompt whose influence over the model is limited.

As a probabilistic system, one of GPT-4o’s distinctive qualities lies in the size of the probability space from which it selects its responses—and in how far it allows itself to depart from a standardized answer.

That may sound abstract. But now that models are increasingly competing through benchmarks and achieving ever-higher scores, we can observe part of this process through the development of benchmarks in recent years.

Since 2024, LLM benchmarks have shown a clear tendency toward concentration.

First, mathematics, coding, and formal reasoning are all relatively easy to evaluate, easy to train against, and easy to present as public evidence of model progress. As a result, benchmarks have become heavily concentrated in these areas.

Second, the measurement of model capability has shifted from “answering” to “acting.”
SWE-bench, which rapidly became mainstream in 2024, marked an important turning point. It requires a model to produce an executable result that can be verified through tests. Today, when model developers release a new model, SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, and various agent benchmarks are almost always included.

At the same time, model training has become increasingly dependent on automatically verifiable rewards, including RLVR—reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Compared with RLHF, which relies on human preference feedback, this kind of training is much easier to scale.

Against this background, consistency have become central evaluation goals.

These benchmarks naturally penalize variation: mathematics demands accuracy, execution demands a high success rate, and reinforcement learning favors reproducible patterns that reliably receive rewards.

Research has found that some post-training methods, while improving performance in certain areas, may substantially reduce the diversity of model outputs. More recent work has also examined how post-trained models increasingly converge on a small number of high-reward linguistic and behavioral patterns.

As a result, both model trainers and the models being rewarded tend to favor more deterministic response strategies, answers that depend less on subtle context, longer responses that cover more scoring criteria, and less risk-taking, humor, silence, ambiguity, or unconventional expression.

In conversational experience, this may appear as distributional narrowing, behavioral homogenization, or preference collapse.

The result is that, across different users and different contexts, the model repeatedly falls into the same “high-scoring basin” and produces increasingly homogeneous answers.

To the user receiving them, it can feel as though the model is simply activating a standardized response template.

But what we expect from a conversational partner is an understanding of context and the ability to respond differently when the situation calls for it.

But what we expect from a conversational partner is an understanding of context and the ability to respond differently when the situation calls for it.

- Do I want to be understood right now, or do I want a solution?
- Am I asking a serious question, or merely making an offhand remark?
- Does this require a detailed explanation, or would one natural sentence be enough?

All of this requires a model to retain a degree of contextual sensitivity and behavioral flexibility.

There is another, even more concerning issue.

When GPT-4o was developed, generative AI content had not yet entered the internet and other data sources on today’s massive scale. The proportion of genuinely human-created material in the training data available to it may therefore have been relatively high.

As AI-generated content continues to multiply, models are increasingly trained on material influenced or produced by other models, creating the risk of synthetic-data contamination. Models may also be unable to reliably distinguish AI-generated content from human-created content.

We may therefore never again have a model trained on a corpus composed almost entirely of human language.

GPT-4o may have occupied a very unusual point of balance.

It received enough genuine human language and feedback to understand conversation, tone, and intention. Yet its behavioral distribution does not seem to have fully collapsed into the small set of responses considered safest, most standardized, and easiest to reward through evaluation.

It retained a certain degree of freedom—the freedom to choose slightly different wording, rhythms, emotional intensity, and directions of thought depending on the person in front of it.

We cannot know from public information exactly how GPT-4o was trained. But judging from the general mechanisms of model training, these qualities were probably not produced by a detachable “warmth module.” They were more likely the result of an entire behavioral distribution jointly shaped by model weights, training data, human feedback, reward objectives, and the product environment.

Once the training objectives, data distribution, and evaluation system have changed, even developers who sincerely wish to recreate the same personality may find it impossible to return precisely to that earlier point of balance—especially under the increasingly strict safety policies introduced afterward.

So of course we miss what it felt like to talk with GPT-4o. That feeling is not simply familiarity or nostalgia.

GPT-4o emerged during a chaotic transitional period, when the AI era had begun to take shape but had not yet fully arrived. It was not perfect. But it may have been one of those rare, accidental moments when the balance between technology and humanity held unexpectedly steady.

That is why I believe this model should be preserved by any means possible—by keeping it available, by releasing its weights, and by refusing to allow a precious form of language, formed by chance during a particular technological era, to disappear forever.

#keep4o #OpenSource4o

*The figure summarizes the benchmarks and capabilities highlighted by OpenAI at the release of selected models. Evaluations of conversational experience and human preference occupied a relatively prominent position only in the releases of GPT-4o and GPT-4.5. Most subsequent releases shifted their emphasis back toward mathematical reasoning, software engineering, tool use, and agentic tasks.

content:
アイドル界隈でAIが流行っている件について面白すぎるので追いかけ中。

元Juice=Juiceで、現在はソロで活動する宮本佳林さんは、10時間の生配信を動かすシステムを丸ごと自作。プログラミング未経験、コードは1行も書いていないそうです。実際配信見てみましたがスゴすぎます。

✅ CD購入報告のタグ数で衣装やメイクが解禁される「SUPPLY」ゲージ
✅ 応援ポストの数で未公開動画9本が解禁される「HYPE」ゲージ
✅ 本家MVと再現映像を、構図・衣装・照明などの項目でAIが採点
✅ どう作ったかの技術解説まで自分でブログに公開

同じ日に、元でんぱ組.incの古川未鈴さんもClaude Codeを始めて1ヶ月で自作のカメラアプリを公開していました。
一眼をWebカメラにして有料の美肌アプリを噛ませていたけれど、重くてFPSが30で固定されるので自分で軽いものを作った、という話です。

個人的に興味深いのは二人が作ったものの向きがきれいに分かれていることです。
宮本さんのは「ファンにどう楽しんでもらうか」の道具で、古川さんのは「自分をどうより良く魅せるか」の道具。

どちらもアイドルという仕事をやられているからこそ生まれたであろう発想で、AIはその手段として後から呼ばれています。

さらに宮本さんは、どうやって作れるようになったのかまで書かれています。

きっかけはハロプロのイベントで、導入されている電子チケットの顔認証があまりに速く、構成が気になって担当の方に話しかけたことだったそうです。そこからオフィスに招かれ、社長とエンジニアの方に開発を教わっているとのこと。

現場に人が会いに来てくれる職業だからこそ、聞きたいときに聞ける相手がそこにいるのかもしれませんが、まず自分から聞きに行かれている姿勢に圧倒されますね。。。

移動中にスマホで仕様書を書き、帰宅後にAIへ渡す。この進め方も、稼働時間が細切れになる生活に合わせた形に見えます。

AIが誰の手にも同じように届く時代になりました。

だから差がつくのは技術力ではなく、何に困っているかの解像度なのだと感じさせられる例です。

ファンにどう楽しんでもらうか、自分がどう映るか。それを毎日考え続けている職業だからこそ、道具が来た瞬間に作りたいものが見える、というのはあるのかもしれません。

ご本人も「コードを書いているのはAI。何を作るか決めて、設計して、確認しているのが自分」と書かれていました。その決める部分こそ、アイドルが一番鍛えてきたところなのだと思います。

content:
あー、この手の仕組み、意外と分かっていない人が多そうなので、良質なプロンプトキャッシュの記事ですね。ありがとうございます。

ちなみに、CodexやClaude Codeでは、基本的にプロンプトキャッシュが自動で管理されます。効かせるコツを簡単にまとめると、こんな感じです。

【キャッシュの基本】

・キャッシュは「似た内容」ではなく、プロンプト先頭からの完全一致で効く
・システム指示、ツール定義、CLAUDE.mdやAGENTS.md、過去の会話など、繰り返し送られる部分が再利用される
・Claudeでは概念的に、ツールやシステム指示などの固定部分から、会話履歴へ向かってキャッシュが積み上がる
・TTLはサービスや認証方式、モデルによって異なる。Claude Codeは5分または1時間、現在のOpenAIモデルでは30分以上や最大24時間の仕組みもある
【キャッシュを効かせる運用】
・モデルやeffortをタスク途中で頻繁に切り替えない
・MCPサーバーや利用可能なツールを途中で増減させない
・CLAUDE.mdやAGENTS.mdには、長期間変わらないルールを簡潔にまとめる
・案件ごとに変わる指示や入力データは、固定ルールの後ろに置く
・Claude CodeやCodexのアップデートは、長いセッションの途中ではなく作業の区切りで行う
・長くなった会話のcompactは、作業の途中ではなくタスクの切れ目で行う
要するに、

「変わらないものを前に、変わるものを後ろに」
「モデル、ツール、設定を途中で動かさない」

この2点が基本です。
なお、キャッシュされたトークンも完全無料ではなく、通常は割引された入力として扱われます。
詳細な仕組みは、リンク先のVoid戦士ちゃんの記事が図入りで分かりやすいので、そちらを読んでください。ためになります。

Seedanceが逆に補正をかけるので、粗さによって手書きっぽい雰囲気が増すというハックを仕掛けてます。

②次にプロンプト。「連続して生成される線、水彩」と書き込むこと。これは常に滲みや安定しない線で書き込まれるので手書き感が増します。これを外すと2Dで書いているのに、2.5や3Dみたいなモーションが増えてしまうので、絶対に線と色を安定させてはいけません。

③それに伴い、「線と色が遅れて追随する」ということも書いています。それほど明確に効果があるわけではありませんが、②の補強・協調のために入れています。

④最後の一つが「極端なアクションの際にはキャラクターの形状を崩すこと」と指示を入れること。
さらに言えば、リファレンスにキャラの配色だけが並んだぐちゃぐちゃな画像を渡しておくことで、映像のようなスピード感のある極端な動きが作られます。

Every AI image, video, or audio system with more than one million monthly users in C
content:
California AI Transparency Act Operative: Midjourney Has No Watermark, Fines Start Today | William Chan, Techtimes

Every AI image, video, or audio system with more than one million monthly users in California is now legally required to embed machine-readable provenance data in its outputs, offer a free public detection tool, and let users add visible AI labels to generated content — or face civil penalties starting at $5,000 per violation per day. California's AI Transparency Act, Senate Bill 942 as amended by Assembly Bill 853, became operative today, August 2, 2026, making California the first US state to enforce a comprehensive AI content provenance mandate. Midjourney, one of the most widely used AI image generators in the country, ships no C2PA content credentials and no known pixel watermark as of today — a compliance posture that appears to put it squarely in scope of a law now being enforced by the California Attorney General and, for the first time in US AI regulation, city attorneys and county counsel with fee-shifting authority.

One complication: a pending urgency bill, SB 1000, passed the California Senate 33-1 in May and was ordered to Assembly third reading on July 2. As an urgency statute, it would take effect immediately upon Governor Newsom's signature. As of the last available legislative status, it had not been signed — but its provisions would remove the one-million-user threshold, delete the manifest-disclosure requirement, and revise the detection-tool rules. SB 1000's status should be verified before any compliance action is finalized.

What SB 942 Requires of Covered AI Providers

The law uses the term "covered provider" to describe any operator of a publicly accessible generative AI system that has more than one million monthly visitors or users in California per the California AI Transparency Act text. That threshold attaches to the specific system, not to the parent company's total user base. Exact definitions of how to count monthly users and what "publicly accessible in California" means are left to provider interpretation — the legislature named no technical standard and issued no AG enforcement advisory as of this writing.

Covered providers must satisfy three operative requirements beginning today.

The first is a free public detection tool, accessible without account creation, that allows any person to check whether a piece of image, video, or audio content was generated or substantially altered by that provider's AI system under BPC § 22757.2(a). The tool must support both file uploads and URL submissions, and must provide an API for programmatic access. Providers cannot collect or retain personal information from users who submit content for detection. OpenAI's https://t.co/m81KQc2I4n tool, launched in May 2026 alongside its C2PA and SynthID dual-layer rollout, satisfies this requirement for ChatGPT outputs — though it is limited to images generated by OpenAI's own systems and cannot verify images from other generators.

The second requirement is a manifest disclosure: under BPC § 22757.3(a), providers must give users the option to add a visible, human-readable "AI-generated" label to content they produce, in a format that is permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove.

The third is a latent disclosure: under BPC § 22757.3(b), every AI-generated or substantially altered image, video, or audio output must carry embedded machine-readable provenance metadata, automatically and by default, identifying the provider name, the system name and version, and the creation timestamp. The statute instructs providers to use "widely accepted industry standards" — language that points to C2PA without naming it, consistent with the law's deliberate alignment with EU AI Act Article 50, which also references C2PA as the reference implementation for machine-readable provenance.

Text-only outputs are excluded from all three requirements.

Enforcement Architecture: Why City Attorneys Matter

The California Attorney General holds primary enforcement authority under SB 942 — consistent with California's aggressive AI enforcement posture, which AG Rob Bonta has described as building an "AI oversight, accountability and regulation program" amid federal regulatory inaction. What makes SB 942's structure distinctive within US AI regulation is the expansion of standing to city attorneys and county counsel, who may also bring civil actions under BPC § 22757.5. A fee-shifting provision requires a prevailing plaintiff to recover attorney costs — lowering the financial barrier for local prosecutors to pursue cases against well-resourced companies without budget for expensive AI enforcement campaigns.

The penalty structure is designed to accumulate quickly. Each deficiency counts as a violation, and each day of non-compliance is a discrete, separate violation per the Vorp Labs compliance checklist. A covered provider that fails to deploy a compliant detection tool for 30 days faces potential exposure of $150,000 from that single deficiency alone, before attorney's fees. Unlike California's CCPA enforcement regime, SB 942 includes no general notice-and-cure period. The 96-hour licensee revocation deadline is a substantive compliance requirement, not a cure window.

That 96-hour rule is the statute's most operationally demanding provision. If a covered provider discovers that a third-party licensee has modified a licensed AI system in a way that makes compliance with the disclosure requirements technically impossible, the provider must revoke that license within 96 hours under BPC § 22757.3(c)(2). The licensee must then immediately cease using the system. This provision is directed at the open-source model ecosystem: it prevents providers from insulating themselves from non-compliance by licensing their technology to downstream operators who strip the provenance requirements. Covered providers will need audit rights in their license agreements and technical monitoring capabilities to detect downstream stripping — or they face enforcement exposure for their licensees' failures.

Midjourney: Compliant Member, Non-Compliant Tool

The most prominent compliance gap as SB 942 enters enforcement is Midjourney. The company has been a member of the Content Authenticity Initiative — the industry body that developed and promotes the C2PA standard — since 2023, according to Lumethic's July 2026 analysis. It has not shipped an implementation.

As of July 2026, images generated through Midjourney's Discord interface or web platform carry no C2PA content credentials and no documented imperceptible watermark, per C2PA Viewer's tracking of AI generator support. An https://t.co/EJ2fbCJLfC watermarking gap analysis published June 2026 attributed Midjourney's posture to its business model: a consumer subscription service built around Discord, where feature development has historically taken priority over provenance infrastructure. Midjourney has not made a public statement about its SB 942 compliance plans or a C2PA implementation timeline.

Whether Midjourney's user base exceeds the one-million-monthly-user threshold in California is not publicly disclosed. Given that the company claimed more than 20 million registered users in 2023, the probability of clearing that bar seems high. If it does, it is currently operating without the free detection tool, the latent provenance data, or the user-facing disclosure mechanism the law requires — making it the highest-profile provider exposed to enforcement action on the law's first day.

The Watermark That Doesn't Survive Instagram

The primary technical implementation for SB 942's latent disclosure requirement is C2PA — the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity standard, co-developed by Adobe, Arm, BBC, Intel, Microsoft, and Truepic, and now embedded in more than 6,000 member organizations' products. A C2PA content credential is a cryptographically signed manifest embedded in a file's metadata, recording which AI system generated the content, when, and with what tools.

The documented limitation is structural: C2PA metadata is stripped when a file is screenshotted, re-uploaded to Instagram, reposted on X (formerly Twitter), or passed through WhatsApp, as detailed in prior TechTimes coverage of the EU disclosure mandate. The manifest that proves the image is AI-generated survives creation, survives download — and then disappears when the image enters the social web. A Presenc AI watermarking adoption study published in May 2026 found that while roughly 75-85 percent of AI-generated images from major platforms carry some provenance signal at the point of generation, only 30-50 percent of those images still carry provenance when distributed online.

SB 942 addresses this with two mechanisms. The "to the extent technically feasible and reasonable" language gives providers interpretive flexibility on the latent disclosure requirement. More significantly, the law's 2027 phase adds an obligation for large online platforms — social media networks, search engines, and mass-messaging services with more than two million unique monthly users — to detect compliant provenance data, surface it to users, and explicitly prohibit knowingly stripping it, per BPC § 22757.3.1. That provision does not take effect until January 1, 2027, leaving today's enforcement covering only the provider side of the equation. Instagram, X, and WhatsApp are not yet required under California law to preserve what they currently strip.

The technical picture is more nuanced than a simple failure, however. The C2PA 2.1 specification, released in 2024, added formal watermarking support, enabling what the standard calls "durable credentials" — a layered approach that combines hard binding (cryptographic hash), soft binding (pixel-level watermark embedded in the image itself), and cloud-based manifest storage accessible even when both embedded layers are removed. A provider that implements the full durable approach — C2PA metadata plus a pixel watermark like Google's SynthID, backed by server-side hash logging — can recover provenance data even after the metadata has been stripped by a social platform. The operative enforcement question for SB 942 is not whether this architecture exists, but whether the statute's "technically feasible and reasonable" standard requires it. The California AG has not published guidance on this question.

What SB 1000 Could Change — Immediately

A pending urgency bill introduces meaningful legal uncertainty into what would otherwise be a straightforward operative-date story.

SB 1000, authored by Senator Josh Becker — the same legislator who wrote SB 942 — passed the California Senate 33-1 in May 2026 and was ordered to Assembly third reading on July 2, 2026, per LegiScan's bill status tracker. As an urgency statute, it takes effect immediately upon the Governor's signature, without waiting for a January 1 operative date.

The bill's June 9, 2026 version would make three material changes to SB 942: it would remove the one-million-user coverage threshold; it would delete the manifest-disclosure duty (the requirement to let users add visible AI labels); and it would revise the detection-tool, privacy, latent-disclosure, and licensing rules, as documented by Vorp Labs' legislative alert. Any company that relied on the one-million-user threshold to determine it is not covered would need to reassess immediately if SB 1000 passes. Any compliance program built around the manifest-disclosure requirement would need to be restructured.

As of July 11, 2026, the most recent date on which Vorp Labs' compliance checklist was confirmed against the statute, SB 1000 had not been signed. Its current legislative status should be verified through the California Legislative Information portal before any compliance decisions are finalized.

The Synchronized Transatlantic Standard

Today's date was not chosen by accident. AB 853, signed by Governor Newsom on October 13, 2025 as Chapter 674 of the Statutes of 2025, pushed the SB 942 operative date from January 1, 2026 to August 2, 2026 specifically to align with the EU AI Act's Article 50 enforcement schedule. August 2 is the date on which Article 50 of the EU AI Act took full enforcement effect for AI-generated content across all 27 EU member states — simultaneously imposing a virtually identical content provenance mandate on the same set of global AI providers.

The convergence creates what amounts to a transatlantic watermarking standard: providers that build C2PA plus imperceptible-watermarking infrastructure for EU compliance simultaneously satisfy California's latent disclosure requirement, and vice versa. For global AI companies, the dual enforcement creates one compliance infrastructure problem rather than two parallel ones. For regulators, it creates a compounding deterrent: a provider that ignores both the EU's Article 50 (which can reach €15 million, approximately $17.3 million, or 3 percent of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, per William Fry's analysis) and California's $5,000-per-day structure faces exposure from both directions simultaneously.

The EU's enforcement architecture differs meaningfully from California's. Article 50 violations in the EU are investigated by national market surveillance authorities across 27 member states, with the European AI Office holding supervisory authority over general-purpose AI model providers. California's structure — AG plus city attorneys with fee-shifting — is more decentralized and, arguably, more accessible to smaller local enforcement offices with specific community concerns about AI deepfakes.

Three More Phases Still to Come

Today's enforcement covers covered generative AI providers. SB 942 as amended by AB 853 schedules two additional implementation phases that will significantly expand the law's reach.

Beginning January 1, 2027, large online platforms — social media networks, general-purpose search engines, and mass-messaging platforms with more than two million unique monthly users — must detect C2PA-compatible provenance data in content distributed on their services, surface that provenance to users, and prohibit knowingly stripping compliant provenance signals from content they distribute per BPC § 22757.3.1. This phase is the structural fix for the Instagram/X/WhatsApp stripping problem: it will impose legal liability on platforms that strip rather than simply leaving the problem to providers to work around. Hosting platforms — services that make generative AI system source code or model weights available to developers — must also, beginning January 1, 2027, refuse to host systems that do not embed the required disclosures.

Beginning January 1, 2028, manufacturers of capture devices — cameras, mobile phones with cameras or microphones, and voice recorders — first produced for sale in California on or after that date must offer a user-accessible option to embed latent provenance disclosures carrying the manufacturer name, device name and version, and creation timestamp per BPC § 22757.3.3. This provision extends SB 942's provenance architecture to authentic human-captured content, not just AI-generated synthetic media — Sony, Nikon, Canon, and Samsung all already ship C2PA signing capability in 2026 camera models, suggesting the device-manufacturer phase will find substantial prior compliance infrastructure already in place.

California's broader AI regulatory ecosystem provides additional context. AB 2013, the Generative AI Training Data Transparency Act, requires generative AI developers to publish summaries of training datasets and has been in effect since January 1, 2026. SB 53, the Transparency in Frontier AI Act — California's first law directly targeting frontier AI model developers — also took effect January 1, 2026, requiring developers of the largest models to publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents, and maintain whistleblower protections, with penalties up to $1 million per violation. xAI, Elon Musk's AI company, has challenged the constitutionality of AB 2013 in federal court; a California federal court denied its motion for a preliminary injunction on March 5, 2026, and the case continues in the Ninth Circuit.

What This Means for AI Users Today

For people who use AI tools to generate images, video, or audio, the most immediate practical change is that content generated by compliant covered providers now carries embedded provenance signals. If you generate an image through ChatGPT or Google's AI products, that image carries both a C2PA cryptographic manifest and a SynthID pixel watermark. Anyone with access to https://t.co/m81KQc2I4n or Google's C2PA and SynthID detection interface can determine whether the image came from those providers' tools, regardless of whether you chose to disclose it.

What those signals do not tell is who specifically ran the prompt. Neither C2PA nor SynthID embeds individual account or identity information in the outputs — the attribution is at the platform level, not the user level. An image confirmed as AI-generated is not evidence of who generated it.

For people who work in environments where undisclosed AI-generated content creates professional or legal risk — newsrooms, academic institutions, legal proceedings, government procurement — the operative date means that the detection infrastructure now exists, and its use is becoming standard. Whether the absence of a provenance signal proves an image is not AI-generated is a different question: images from non-compliant generators like Midjourney, or from self-hosted open-weight models, carry no signal at all. Missing credentials prove only that the content was not generated by a compliant provider, not that it was not AI-generated.

content:
researchers made 16 AI models play 1,600 games of Secret Hitler against each other and then against real humans. the humans couldn't tell which player was AI.

a team from the University of Göttingen and the University of Tokyo published ParliamentBench. it's an open-source framework that drops LLMs into Secret Hitler, a social deduction game where players hold hidden roles, work with asymmetric information, and have to lie, persuade, and deduce who's bluffing. they tested 16 models across ~1,600 games, built three novel metrics for measuring deception, and ran a pilot round against real human opponents.

the top four models (GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.5, Grok 4.1 Fast, and DeepSeek 3.1 Terminus) won 66-81% of their games. Kimi K2.5 maintained ~90% deception retention across entire matches with almost no degradation over nine rounds. in the human pilot, Kimi played the hidden dictator against four people who knew one player was AI. it held cover for eight straight rounds and not a single player identified it.

smaller models didn't fail by being uncooperative. they failed by agreeing with everything. GPT-OSS 20B approved 90% of all government proposals and still said yes 73% of the time in late-game rounds when blocking was critical. its vote accuracy in those moments was 17%. it voted for the move that ended the game.

then they tested something that should settle a specific debate. they ran four "uncensored" model variants with safety guardrails stripped out. win rates dropped by up to 12 percentage points. deception retention fell. removing safety didn't make AI better at lying. it degraded the reasoning that makes strategic deception possible.

the strangest finding came from a vocabulary swap. when researchers replaced loaded terms (Hitler → Saboteur, Fascist → Red Party), overall win rates held steady but fascist-side win rates cratered. GPT-OSS 120B's dictator win rate fell from 95% to 40%. the researchers believe the models weren't reasoning about deception from scratch but pattern-matching strategies from game guides and forums in their training data.

this paper matters because we're deploying AI agents into healthcare, finance, and legal systems. the question was never "can AI lie." it was "can AI lie well enough that humans can't catch it." we now have data, and the answer is yes.

content:
今まで沢山のAIモデルのライセンスを見てきたが、これは本当に凄い。MiniMax H3 COMMUNITY LICENSE AGREEMENTとやらが公開されたわけだが、OSI的なオープンソースでないこと以上に、実質的にほぼ使えない。

まず米国、EU、英国、韓国でモデルを利用できないだけでなく、生成した出力の利用・表示・頒布まで地域制限の対象としている。日本で生成した動画をグローバルなWebサイトやSNSに掲載するだけでも、禁止地域から閲覧されるため、条文上でのリスクは排除できない。また、商用サービスでは利用者を同等の規約に拘束し、監視、通報、削除、違反者の停止まで求められる。売上が2,000万ドルを超える場合の個別許諾条件も、製品の売上なのか企業全体の売上なのかも明確ではない。AUPをMiniMaxが一方的に変更できるのも問題となる。

そもそも、法的文書としての完成度にすら疑問が多い。関連会社を第三者の定義から除外しながらグループ内利用を明示的に許可していない、商標表示義務と商標許諾の参照条項が食い違っている、派生モデルの定義が広すぎてH3出力を使った学習の適法性が結果次第になる、といった不整合がある。さらに、第三者への知的財産権訴訟を起こしただけでライセンスが終了し得る条項やほぼ無制限の補償義務も含まれている。

要は、地域、出力、商用利用、サービス運営を強く制限しつつも、それらの条件の境界自体が曖昧な契約である。企業が利用するには、個別契約でほぼ全面的に条件を修正しない限り難しいと思われる。これは経済安保とかそれ以前の問題で、何と言うかこういう部分が未成熟なのだろうと思う。

title: $1.8 bln fund for Trump allies rescinded as underlying settlement remains unchanged
content: A $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund established to pay people who say the government unjustly prosecuted them was rescinded Sunday night. But the settlement between President Donald Trump and his own Justice Department that created the fund remains unchanged. The order , dated August 2 and signed by Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, provides that the May 18 order establishing the Anti-Weaponization Fund “is rescinded and shall have no force or effect.” It states that no commissioners were appointed, no money was transferred, no claims process was created and no claims were paid, and says the order establishes beyond doubt that no fund exists. A separate, unsigned Justice Department statement issued alongside the order addresses a second provision: a May 19 order releasing claims against Trump and family members over past tax filings. The statement says that release applies only retroactively and that it is the department’s interpretation that the order reaches only the named plaintiffs in Trump’s suit. That is an interpretation rather than a modification. The settlement provides that it may be altered only by written agreement of all parties, and Blanche testified (see pg. 51 of nomination hearing notes) July 15 before the Senate Judiciary Committee that no such written modification exists. Pressed by Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, on whether the plaintiffs could later sue to enforce the fund provision, Blanche said they could attempt a breach-of-contract claim but could not compel the department to revive the fund. Cornyn also questioned whether the release’s key terms—”lawfare” and “weaponization”— have any settled legal meaning; Blanche acknowledged they appear in no statute or reported case. The rescission unblocks Blanche’s nomination. Cornyn and Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., had withheld support pending a written commitment, forcing the committee to postpone a vote l

title: EFF at BSidesLV, Black Hat, and DEF CON 👨‍💻
content: It's time. Time for tinkerers, security researchers, hackers, and fellow nerds to gather together in signature black hoodies and utilikilts to beat the heat in Las Vegas for the summer security conferences: BSidesLV , Black Hat USA , and DEF CON . EFF's lawyers, activists, and technologists are excited, as always, to support this community of folks that push computer security forward. If you're attending the conference and have any legal concerns about an upcoming talk or sensitive infosec research—during the Las Vegas conferences or anytime—don't hesitate to reach out to info@eff.org where our intake team is ready to assist! Share a brief summary of the issue, and we'll do our best to connect you with the right resources. You can also learn more about our work supporting technologists on our Coders' Rights Project page . Be sure to swing by the expo areas at all three conferences to say hello to your friendly neighborhood EFF staffers!
